brief: My balcony is partial shade with moderate moisture, and one dog lives in the household. A half-shady balcony with a small dog who likes to nibble at plants.

design.site_summary: A partial shade balcony with moderate moisture, designed safely for a household with a small nibbling dog.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme is structured vertically with trailing plants cascading from the railing, upright structural perennials occupying the mid-layer containers against the back wall, and a pet-accessible ground layer at floor level near the balcony entrance.
design.combination_logic: The plants combine fine delicate foliage with bold architectural leaves, offering contrasts in texture from sword-like fronds to soft grassy blades, while maintaining a calming green and silver palette with subtle seasonal white blooms.

zones.placement: on the north-facing railing, receiving indirect ambient light and 2 hours of gentle morning sun

plants.why: Thrives in partial shade, drapes gracefully over container edges, and produces charming star-shaped flowers.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides a soft floral accent and cascading habit that breaks the rigid line of the balcony railing.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil feels dry.
Feed with a balanced liquid fertilizer every two weeks during summer.
Trim back leggy stems after the main flowering flush in mid-summer.

zones.placement: against the interior balcony wall, receiving bright indirect light with no direct harsh sun

plants.why: Adapts exceptionally well to partial shade and moderate moisture, adding lush architectural volume.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as the structural anchor of the mid-layer, contrasting upright fronds against the trailing and ground-level plants.

maintenance: Keep the potting mix consistently moist but never waterlogged.
Remove old, tattered fronds in early spring to make way for new growth.
Repot into a slightly larger container every two years.

zones.placement: on the sheltered balcony floor near the sliding door, receiving filtered light and full pet accessibility

plants.why: Completely non-toxic to dogs, grass-like appearance that satisfies the pet's urge to nibble without harm.
plants.role_in_combination: Introduces fine-textured vertical blades at floor level that contrast sharply with the broader leaves above.

maintenance: Water frequently to ensure the soil remains evenly moist.
Divide the clump in spring if it becomes overcrowded in the low tray.
No chemical fertilizers should be used since the dog interacts closely with this zone.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture levels across all containers with a finger test
care_instructions.frequency: twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Apply a dilute organic liquid fertilizer to the hanging and mid-layer containers
Clear away dead fronds from the fern and cut back spent flower stems on the bellflower
care_instructions.frequency: once at the end of the season

care_cautions: Overwatering the Japanese Sweet Flag in the ground-layer tray can lead to stagnation, so ensure excess water drains freely.
The Serbian Bellflower in the hanging basket is exposed to drying winds and may dry out much faster than the mid-layer containers.
While the Japanese Sweet Flag is safe for the dog to nibble, monitor the pet to prevent it from uprooting the entire plant from the shallow tray.
design.pet_safety_note: The design strictly excludes toxic species and dedicates a specific ground-level tray to non-toxic grass-like plants, ensuring the household dog can safely explore and nibble without risk of poisoning.
